The stable/2024.1 and 2024.2 backports each squash the original change and the follow-up regression fix for LP #2105383 into one commit. The unit tests had to be adapted, so the reviewer should check that the SRU package carries both parts and passes the tests. The original change alone regressed the redirect-type calculation.
The backports stop at stable/2024.1. Ubuntu series that ship older Neutron (for example Yoga on Jammy) have no upstream backport, so the fix may not be available for every series that needs the SRU.

comments.author: whershberger
comments.body:
There are two standing issues with these patches:

- get_global_pool_hard_max_size parses /proc/sys/vm/max_map_count incorrectly, resulting in the default value being used unconditionally
- The default value returned by get_global_pool_hard_max_size is UINT_MAX; a better/conservative choice would be the kernel's default max_map_count (65530)

We've submitted upstream patches to resolve both of these issues; neither have been merged to qemu's master yet.

https://lists.gnu.org/archive/html/qemu-devel/2026-10/msg04337.html

blockers.summary: Regression mentioned: "…to 64. This could produce a performance regression for some users, as the performance bottleneck of this cap was significant enoug…" (whershberger)

The backported patches parse /proc/sys/vm/max_map_count incorrectly in get_global_pool_hard_max_size, so the default value is always used. The fix is not actually effective until the parsing patch is added, and the upstream patch is not yet merged.
The default hard max returned when the sysctl cannot be read is UINT_MAX, effectively no limit. A conservative default (65530) is needed, and that upstream patch is not yet merged.

The new code reads /proc/sys/vm/max_map_count, which needs a libvirt AppArmor profile change (tracked in a separate libvirt bug). A versioned Breaks/dependency in qemu is also needed to force the libvirt upgrade. Both are still unconfirmed, and without them confined guests may break or misbehave.

Even with the fix, crashes remain possible with very large vCPU/thread counts, and the pool cap does not bound total coroutines. A crash was reproduced under the noble limit with 255 vCPUs, and the reviewer asked what happens when the limit is hit. This is a partial mitigation, and its justification versus raising the sysctl is contested.

Follow-up changes (string-parsing fix and lower default max pool size) must be tracked and applied to all newer supported releases. The coroutine pool behavior also differs between the series, and the upstream patches are unmerged, so the SRU delta may diverge from upstream.
